title: Conditional Extreme Quantile Treatment Effects with Sparse Tail Scales at Dense Profiles
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier: the advertised all-dimensional matched minimax frontier remains open; independent validity gate confirmed no bounded field-level repair.
gap_reasons: The advertised all-dimensional sharp minimax rate, matched estimator/interval, and consistency boundary remain explicitly open; the delivered p=2 benchmark and loose bracket are materially weaker than that headline object.

Resolve the rare-event dense-profile radius in oeq:profile-score and validate it with the exact support-mixture cross-products required by oeq:mixture-transition. Use those matched bounds to complete oeq:joint-frontier, including an observable estimator, honest interval, and explicit consistency boundary.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived observed-arm reduction, two-criterion universal lower floors, a matched p=2,s=1 benchmark, and a loose general bracket. D0.5 found that the all-dimensional matched minimax frontier advertised by the topic was still open; the profile-score, support-mixture transition, and joint-frontier nodes need independent derivation. An independent validity gate confirmed that this is the unresolved headline program rather than a bounded repair, while the math referee passed the proved pieces.
tldr: Conditional extreme-wage effects at a dense covariate profile require extrapolating beyond observed ranks while estimating a dense loading of sparse armwise log-tail scales. Two same-class constructions show that both minimax expected absolute error and minimax maximal expected length of uniformly \(90\%\)-honest connected intervals obey the Hall target-depth floor and the disclosed-support sparse-profile floor. The upper route through multithreshold rare-event profile-score inversion is only a candidate route because \(\text{oeq:profile-score}\) remains open. The exact joint rate, transition logarithm, observable threshold, and consistency boundary remain answer-open, as do the positive-overlap support-mixture kernel and same-envelope recentering test.
gap: Conditional causal extreme-QTE theory is fixed-dimensional, sparse extreme-quantile regression supplies upper prediction bounds without causal or dense-functional converses, and honest scalar tail inference omits covariate profiles.
fill: The project derives the observable profile radius and exact support-mixture affinity, then optimizes the intermediate threshold to match point risk and honest interval length and to state the full consistency boundary.
